data.hypothesis: An explicit OpenMP SIMD directive over the contiguous c dimension may improve the already measured serial r-k-c traversal by making vectorization across each B/C row more explicit. This keeps k ascending for each output element and uses no additional threads, isolating SIMD as a follow-up to the serial traversal result; the previous row-parallel result motivates separate thread experiments but does not establish a SIMD benefit. Clearing C first preserves overwrite behavior.

memory_lessons.applicability: This SIMD-only follow-up should be compared with the serial r-k-c measurements; the row-parallel measurement is useful context but does not isolate SIMD.
memory_lessons.claim: The serial r-k-c program was valid on all six checked cases, with n=1024 samples 0.076063603, 0.076956635, and 0.076168533 seconds. A row-parallel r-k-c program was also valid, with mean 0.009476690818181815 seconds. These results motivate testing SIMD separately and do not establish its effect.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this serial SIMD variant on all official sizes and compare repeated native n=1024 timings against the serial r-k-c result.

data.notes: This is a serial r-k-c traversal with only an explicit SIMD directive added across c relative to the prior serial variant. Output is zeroed before accumulation, k remains ascending for each output, and a generic-size fallback is retained. The supplied prior candidates were valid; no unsuccessful variant is present in the provided observations. This proposal has no new correctness or timing result; controller measurements should check the fixed oracle tolerance on all official sizes and repeat native n=1024 timings.
transformations: Change the r-c-k dot-product loop to a row-wise r-k-c rank-1 update, traversing B and C rows contiguously.
Add an OpenMP SIMD directive to the innermost c loop while retaining ascending-k accumulation for each output element.
Zero the complete output before accumulation and retain a runtime-size fallback; do not create worker threads.
